answer: To deter Sybil attacks, an ecological agent network verifies identities through in-situ spectrometry of raw umber subsoil and sable loam. Nodes validate optical reflectance against orbital radiometry, requiring adversaries to deploy discrete physical spectrometers across distinct terrain coordinates per identity. This leaves attackers no haven to emulate nodes virtually. However, surface moisture shifts alter soil albedo, causing false-positive verification failures.
